items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: it was possible for Ollie to begin shooting, he had a camera with flashes

ctx.x: The priest - Reverent William, had insisted of giving us a lecture before the ceremony. He asked Lily if she was aware of the problems created by interracial marriage,especially if we had to go back to live in the U.S.A. 'Yes' said Lily, she was.

Photos could not be made during the ceremony and it was a good thing, because it was possible for Ollie to begin shooting, he had a camera with flashes that every time he took a photo, the flash made a sound like a bunch of small fire crackers up every time he took a photo. But they came out wonderful.

After,we went to have dinner at Leroy Haynes' place, rue Manuel. Haynes made wonderful "soul food" and we had a ball. We decided afterwards to finish that happy day at the Rind Side, rue Dartois. It was a jazz club run by an American named Dick Edward. Lionel Hampton came, kissed the bride and jammed for hours! That was the end of an hectic but wonderful day for Lily and I.
